name: Lulu
description: A polished Palm Springs staple with a lively dining room, dependable brunch, and a great first-stop energy for guests arriving in town.
darceysTake: Lulu is one of those Palm Springs staples I always feel good recommending, especially if someone is visiting and wants that fun downtown energy. I love the bar for happy hour, the patio for people-watching, and the menu has something for just about everyone. My go-to dishes are the salads, Chicken Piccata, and of course the truffle fries. If you are there on a weekend and the Chicken Pot Pie is available, order it. Make a reservation and ask for a good table - this is one of the best people-watching spots in Palm Springs.
imageAlt: Lulu in Palm Springs
favoriteDish: Truffle fries and the classic brunch plate

name: Giuseppe's
description: Warm, reliable Italian comfort with the kind of neighborhood feel that makes people come back again and again.
darceysTake: Giuseppe's is such a great neighborhood Italian spot, especially when you want something casual, comfortable, and dependable. In season, get there early if you want a bar seat because it fills up fast. The happy hour pizza is a great value, and I love pairing it with the Caesar salad. It is one of those places where you can keep it simple and still leave happy.
imageAlt: Giuseppe's in Palm Springs
favoriteDish: House pasta and a glass of red

name: Palmina by Puglia
description: A spirited Italian favorite with authentic Puglian flavors, a warm host, and the kind of room that makes dinner feel like an occasion.
darceysTake: Palmina feels like dinner with someone who truly loves sharing Italian food. Antonello brings so much pride and personality to the room, and you can feel it in the food, the ingredients, and the way guests are treated. The pizza tastes truly authentic, the pasta is full of flavor, and the espresso martini is a perfect way to end the night. This is a great spot when you want dinner to feel warm, personal, and a little special.
imageAlt: Palmina by Puglia in Palm Springs
happyHour: Ask about current bar and evening specials

name: La Perlita
description: Unfussy, flavorful, and beloved for casual Mexican food that feels like a local recommendation rather than a tourist script.
darceysTake: La Perlita is a great casual Mexican spot when you want good food without making a big production of it. It has that easy local feel, and sometimes that is exactly what you want. My tip is to skip the sugary margarita mix and order the skinny margarita. It is simple, refreshing, and lets the food shine.
imageAlt: La Perlita in Palm Springs

name: Cactus Jack's
description: A desert institution with character, regulars, and the sort of local texture that does not need polishing.
darceysTake: Cactus Jack's is a true local desert classic. It is not fancy, and that is exactly why people love it. The food is good, the prices are fair, and the bar has that fun regulars-and-locals kind of energy. If you sit at the bar, just know the wine pours are generous and the cocktails can be strong - this may be a good night to call an Uber.
imageAlt: Cactus Jack's in Palm Desert

name: California Bistro
description: Easygoing California dining with enough polish for date night and enough comfort for a midweek favorite.
darceysTake: California Bistro has a beautiful dining room and patio, but do not overlook the bar. The big wraparound bar is lively, social, and the service is always great. Their happy hour menu has plenty of good choices, but my favorite is the Blackened Chicken Sandwich. Honestly, it may be my favorite sandwich anywhere in the Valley.
imageAlt: California Bistro in Palm Desert

name: Johnny Costa's
description: A timeless Palm Springs dining room with old Hollywood warmth, confident service, and classic Italian dishes.
darceysTake: Johnny Costa's is a classic Palm Springs dinner spot in the best way. It has that old-school Italian feel, warm service, and a menu that makes you want to settle in and enjoy the night. This is where I would go when I want a proper dinner, not a rushed meal. Book ahead, order something classic, and let it feel like a real night out.
imageAlt: Johnny Costa's in Palm Springs

name: Spencer's
description: Elegant, tucked against the mountain, and still one of the most reliable choices for a special desert meal.
darceysTake: Spencer's has one of my favorite patios in the desert. It is tucked up against the mountain, the atmosphere is beautiful, and the service is always exceptional. I love their wine list - the Dutton Ranch Chardonnay is one of my favorites. If it is your first time, you have to try the Chinese Style Kung Pao Calamari. It is famous for a reason and one of those dishes I find myself craving. Make a reservation during season because Spencer's fills up quickly.
imageAlt: Spencer's in Palm Springs
favoriteDish: Brunch Benedict or filet at dinner

name: Copley's
description: A romantic Palm Springs courtyard restaurant on the historic Cary Grant estate with polished service and memorable desert atmosphere.
darceysTake: Copley's is one of my favorite Palm Springs restaurants for a romantic date night or dinner with friends. John and I celebrated New Year's Eve here, and it was such a special evening. The outdoor courtyard, set on the historic Cary Grant estate, is one of the prettiest dining settings in the desert, especially after sunset when the lights come on. The food is consistently excellent, the cocktails and wine list are wonderful, and the service always makes you feel welcome. If you can, request a courtyard table when you make your reservation. It is the perfect place to relax, celebrate, and enjoy one of the Coachella Valley's most memorable dining experiences.
imageAlt: Copley's in Palm Springs

name: Tyler's
description: A true Palm Springs burger classic, casual in all the right ways and best enjoyed without overthinking it.
darceysTake: Tyler's is the kind of place you do not need to overthink. Go for lunch, order a classic burger, and enjoy the Palm Springs charm of it all. If the patio is open, sit outside. It is casual, simple, and exactly what a good burger spot should be.
imageAlt: Tyler's in Palm Springs
happyHour: Lunch line is part of the ritual

name: Tony's Grill and Bar
description: A comfortable local American pick that works when you want something easy, familiar, and satisfying.
darceysTake: Tony's is a great little neighborhood spot, especially when you want something easy and comfortable. I love sitting at the bar, and their taco salad is huge - definitely big enough to share. Their house wines are really good too. There is no patio, but on a hot summer day, this is the perfect little indoor hideaway.
imageAlt: Tony's Grill and Bar in Palm Springs

name: Bubba's Bones & Brews
description: A casual Cathedral City favorite for barbecue, cold drinks, and easygoing happy-hour energy.
darceysTake: Bubba's is a fun, casual spot for barbecue, drinks, and an easy happy hour. Do not miss the Jalapeno Sausage Wontons - they are so good. The patio is dog friendly too, which makes it a great choice when you want to bring your pup and keep things relaxed.
imageAlt: Bubba's Bones & Brews in Cathedral City
happyHour: A fun casual stop for drinks and bites

name: Bongo Johnny's
description: A relaxed brunch choice with playful energy and a central location that makes it easy with visitors.
darceysTake: Bongo Johnny's is a fun, casual brunch spot when you want something easy in the middle of Palm Springs. It is relaxed, dog-friendly, and great for a low-pressure breakfast or lunch with friends. Go with a laid-back mindset, grab a patio seat if you can, and enjoy the people-watching.
imageAlt: Bongo Johnny's in Palm Springs

name: Cheeky's
description: A stylish brunch favorite with rotating details, bright flavors, and a Palm Springs line that usually tells the story.
darceysTake: Cheeky's is one of those Palm Springs brunch spots people talk about for a reason. The menu is creative, the energy is fun, and the bacon flight is always a conversation starter. Go earlier than you think, especially on weekends, because the line can build quickly. It is worth it if you are in the mood for a brunch that feels very Palm Springs.
imageAlt: Cheeky's in Palm Springs

name: Las Casuelas Terraza
description: A festive standby for visitors who want patio energy, music, margaritas, and a lively downtown evening.
darceysTake: Las Casuelas has several locations in the Valley, but this is my favorite. The outdoor patio is one of the best in the desert, and they often have live music on weekends, so check their schedule before you go. It is great for people-watching, and if you can grab a seat at the palapa bar, you are in for a fun night. The Skinny Cadillac Margaritas are my go-to, the food is always good, and the atmosphere is lively without feeling too fancy.
imageAlt: Las Casuelas Terraza in Palm Springs

name: Mitch's
description: Fresh, elegant, and consistently strong for a night out on El Paseo with clients, friends, or visiting family.
darceysTake: Mitch's is one of my favorite choices when you want a polished night out on El Paseo. It works for date night, visitors, clients, or dinner with friends. The seafood and sushi are always fresh, and I like to ask what just came in before deciding what to order. It is elegant without feeling stiff, and the patio is beautiful when the weather is right.
imageAlt: Mitch's in Palm Desert

name: Cipolline Osteria
description: A refined Italian option for a slower dinner, good wine, and a more intimate desert evening.
darceysTake: Cipolline is a lovely choice when you want a slower Italian dinner with good wine and a cozy, more intimate feel. I like ordering a few starters for the table before pasta so everyone can share and settle in. It is a nice spot for date night or dinner with friends when you want something a little more refined but still warm and comfortable.
imageAlt: Cipolline Osteria in Palm Desert

cardDescription: House-roasted coffee, pastries and an easygoing Palm Springs morning.

name: Indian Canyons Golf Resort
description: A timeless Palm Springs golf experience with mountain views, palms, and that old-desert feeling people hope to find when they come here.
darceysTake: Play Indian Canyons South if you want that postcard-perfect Palm Springs golf experience. The mountain views, palm trees, and old-desert feel are exactly what people picture when they come here. The restaurant is also wonderful for breakfast or lunch, so plan enough time to enjoy it before or after your round.
imageAlt: Indian Canyons Golf Resort in Palm Springs
bestFor: Postcard-perfect Palm Springs scenery
restaurant: A favorite for breakfast and lunch before or after your round.

name: Cimarron Golf Resort
description: A smart, reliable desert round with strong value, approachable play, and views that get especially beautiful late in the day.
darceysTake: Cimarron is one of my favorite value plays in the desert. The course is usually in good condition, the pricing is strong, and it is an easy recommendation when someone wants a fun round without overcomplicating it. Stay after your round if you can - the restaurant and sunset views are worth it.
imageAlt: Cimarron Golf Resort in Cathedral City
bestFor: Good conditions and great prices
restaurant: The restaurant and sunset views make it worth staying after the round.

name: Escena Golf Club
description: A polished Palm Springs course where the architecture, clubhouse, and mountain views all feel deeply connected to the desert lifestyle.
darceysTake: Escena is beautiful from start to finish. The course has big mountain views, and the clubhouse has that mid-century modern Palm Springs look everyone loves. Even if you are not playing, it is worth going for lunch or drinks because the setting is so good. This is a great pick when you want golf to feel stylish and very Palm Springs.
imageAlt: Escena Golf Club in Palm Springs
bestFor: Mid-century clubhouse and big views
restaurant: The clubhouse is part of the experience, with a stylish setting for lunch or drinks.

name: Desert Willow
description: A consistently beautiful Palm Desert golf destination with two courses and the kind of conditioning that makes it easy to recommend.
darceysTake: Desert Willow is one of the easiest golf recommendations in Palm Desert because it is consistently beautiful and so well maintained. With two courses, you have options, and the conditions are almost always excellent. It is a great choice for visitors, clients, or anyone who wants a polished desert golf experience.
imageAlt: Desert Willow in Palm Desert
bestFor: Two course options and immaculate conditions
restaurant: A polished clubhouse setting for a relaxed post-round meal.

name: The Classic Club
description: A bigger, more challenging desert round with a strong practice facility and a clubhouse restaurant that makes it a full-day recommendation.
darceysTake: The Classic Club is a wonderful challenge and a great choice when you want a more serious round. The practice facility is excellent, and Bellatrix makes the whole day feel complete. Even if you are not playing, Bellatrix is a great spot for lunch, dinner, or a post-round drink on the patio.
imageAlt: The Classic Club in Palm Desert
bestFor: A serious round and great practice facility
restaurant: Bellatrix is outstanding, whether you are playing or just meeting for a meal.

name: Indian Canyons
description: Native palm oases, flowing streams and dramatic desert canyon scenery make Indian Canyons one of the signature outdoor experiences in Palm Springs. Choose anything from an easy oasis walk to a more adventurous canyon hike.
cardDescription: Native palm oases, flowing streams and some of Palm Springs' most beautiful canyon scenery.
imageAlt: Indian Canyons in Palm Springs
bestFor: The iconic palm oasis experience
quickInfo: Choose a short walk or go farther
goodToKnow: Check current hours, admission and trail conditions before visiting.

name: Bump and Grind Trail
description: A Palm Desert favorite for anyone looking for a real workout. Bump and Grind climbs into the Santa Rosa Mountains and rewards the effort with sweeping views across the valley.
cardDescription: A local favorite for a workout and sweeping Coachella Valley views.
imageAlt: Bump and Grind Trail in Palm Desert
bestFor: The local workout
goodToKnow: Go early—the trail has very little shade and the desert heats up quickly. The upper vista section closes February 1–April 30; the main lower loop remains the primary hiking experience.

name: Araby Trail
description: Araby Trail combines a challenging desert climb with panoramic Palm Springs views—and a unique look toward the iconic Bob Hope house along the mountainside.
cardDescription: A challenging climb with valley views and a glimpse of iconic Palm Springs architecture.
imageAlt: Araby Trail in Palm Springs
bestFor: The views and architecture hike
goodToKnow: Go early. The climb is exposed with very little shade, and parking near the trailhead is limited.

name: VillageFest
description: A lively Thursday-night Palm Springs tradition with artists, handcrafted goods, music, produce, street performers and food vendors.
darceysTake: If you are visiting Palm Springs on a Thursday night, VillageFest is a must. It is one of our favorite ways to show off Palm Springs to guests or just enjoy an easy night out together. Palm Canyon Drive closes to traffic and fills with local artists, handcrafted goods, live music, street performers, fresh produce and wonderful food vendors. Do not miss The Palm Springs Candle Guys - their candles make fantastic gifts, and they are some of the nicest people you will meet. Come hungry, stroll slowly, try something new, and save room for dessert while you enjoy the live entertainment. VillageFest runs every Thursday evening downtown, typically 6:00 to 10:00 PM October through May and 7:00 to 10:00 PM June through September.
imageAlt: VillageFest in Palm Springs
detail: A weekly downtown street fair along Palm Canyon Drive every Thursday evening.
bestFor: Local makers, food vendors, live music and a classic Palm Springs evening

name: The Living Desert
description: A beloved Palm Desert destination with animals, gardens, walking paths and beautiful desert scenery that works for locals and visiting guests.
darceysTake: The Living Desert is one of my favorite places to take visitors because it feels so uniquely Palm Desert. Go early, especially in the warmer months, so you can enjoy the animals, gardens, and walking paths before the day heats up. Take your time, wear comfortable shoes, and plan a little stop for a cold drink, ice cream, beer, or wine along the way.
imageAlt: The Living Desert in Palm Desert
detail: Wildlife, gardens, trails, exhibits and a uniquely Coachella Valley setting.
bestFor: A classic desert day with visitors or family

name: Desert View Loop / Palm Springs Aerial Tramway
description: Trade the desert floor for cool mountain air. Ride the Palm Springs Aerial Tramway into the San Jacinto Mountains and enjoy an easy loop with beautiful high-country views.
cardDescription: Ride the Tram into cool mountain air for an easy high-country hike.
imageAlt: Desert View Loop / Palm Springs Aerial Tramway in Palm Springs / Mt. San Jacinto
bestFor: The mountain escape
goodToKnow: Temperatures at Mountain Station can be dramatically cooler than the desert floor, so bring an extra layer and check Tram and trail conditions before heading up.

photoCredit.label: Mount San Jacinto State Park trail by Librarybell · CC0

name: Palm Springs Air Museum
description: A fascinating Palm Springs museum with an impressive collection of aircraft, exhibits and stories that bring aviation history to life.
darceysTake: The Palm Springs Air Museum is such a great stop, especially when you want something interesting, memorable, and mostly indoors. The aircraft collection is incredible, but what really makes it special are the stories behind the planes and the volunteers who love sharing them. It is a fun outing with visitors, kids, history lovers, or anyone who appreciates seeing these beautiful aircraft up close. Give yourself enough time to wander the hangars, read the displays, and take it all in.
imageAlt: Palm Springs Air Museum in Palm Springs
detail: Historic aircraft, exhibits, flight history and one of the most unique museums in Palm Springs.
bestFor: A cool indoor outing, aviation history and visiting guests

name: Palm Springs Art Museum
description: A beautiful downtown museum with art, design, architecture and mountain views that make it feel distinctly Palm Springs.
darceysTake: The Palm Springs Art Museum is one of my favorite ways to slow down and enjoy the creative side of the desert. The building, the mountain backdrop, the sculpture, and the exhibitions all feel very Palm Springs. It is perfect before dinner downtown, on a warm afternoon when you want something indoors, or when guests want to see more than just sunshine and palm trees. Check the current exhibitions before you go, and leave a little time to enjoy the architecture and the area around the museum too.
imageAlt: Palm Springs Art Museum in Palm Springs
detail: Modern and contemporary art, sculpture, design, architecture and rotating exhibitions downtown.
bestFor: Art, architecture and a polished downtown Palm Springs outing

name: Sunnylands
description: A beautifully designed Rancho Mirage landmark with modern architecture, desert gardens and a calm, polished setting that feels special without feeling fussy.
darceysTake: Sunnylands is peaceful, beautiful, and such a nice change of pace. Check the tour schedule before you go if you want to see more of the estate, but even just walking the gardens is worth it. Leave time to wander, enjoy the architecture, and take in the mountain views. It is one of those places that feels calm, polished, and very special.
imageAlt: Sunnylands in Rancho Mirage
detail: Historic estate, visitor center, gardens, tours and rotating programming.
bestFor: Architecture, gardens and a peaceful desert outing

name: Coachella Valley Firebirds
description: A fun, lively way to spend an evening in the desert, with great crowd energy and a true local-team feel.
darceysTake: A Firebirds game is such a fun night out, even if you are not a huge hockey person. The crowd energy is great, Acrisure Arena is easy to enjoy, and it feels like a true local experience. Arrive early so parking, food, and getting to your seats all feel easy. It is a great option for families, friends, or visitors who want something lively to do in the evening.
imageAlt: Coachella Valley Firebirds in Palm Desert
detail: Professional hockey at Acrisure Arena with a fun local fan atmosphere.
bestFor: A high-energy night out with family or friends

name: Palm Springs Festival of Lights Parade
description: A beloved Palm Springs holiday tradition with illuminated floats, marching bands, giant balloons and Santa.
darceysTake: One of our favorite holiday traditions is the Palm Springs Festival of Lights Parade. If you are visiting the desert in early December, this is such a fun night downtown. Palm Canyon Drive turns into a festive wonderland with beautifully lit floats, high-energy marching bands, giant holiday balloons and Santa. Get there early, find a good spot along Palm Canyon, and make an evening of it with dinner or a cocktail before the parade begins. Bring a light jacket and a little holiday spirit. The parade is held on the first Saturday in December and draws a big crowd, so arriving early is absolutely worth it.
imageAlt: Palm Springs Festival of Lights Parade in Palm Springs
detail: An annual early-December parade along Palm Canyon Drive.
bestFor: A festive downtown night with family, friends or visiting guests

name: Gelson's Rancho Mirage
description: A polished grocery stop that feels part market, part casual lunch destination and part entertaining shortcut.
darceysTake: Gelson's Rancho Mirage has a wine bar inside the store, which makes shopping feel a little more fun. You can sip while you shop, watch fresh sushi being made, grab a Wolfgang Puck pizza, or stop by the carvery for prime rib or turkey. The deli has some of the most interesting salads, too. I love the idea of doing your shopping and then staying for lunch at the wine bar.

name: World Market
description: A fun Palm Springs stop for unique home pieces, host gifts, pantry finds and small treasures you did not know you needed.
darceysTake: World Market is one of my favorite places in Palm Springs for unique home decor, furniture, gourmet foods, gifts and entertaining essentials from around the world, all at surprisingly approachable prices. Whether you are decorating a new home, refreshing your patio or picking up a thoughtful hostess gift, there is always something interesting to discover. I especially love visiting during the holidays, when the seasonal displays are full of one-of-a-kind finds.
imageAlt: World Market in Palm Springs

darceysTake: When it comes to pest control, I always recommend Mr. Beez Termite & Pest Control. Yes, Barrett, the owner, is my nephew - but I would recommend them even if he was not family. Barrett has built an outstanding reputation throughout the Coachella Valley by doing things the right way: showing up on time, communicating clearly, treating customers with respect and standing behind every job. His team is licensed, bonded and insured, uses family- and pet-conscious treatment methods whenever possible, and backs their work with a 100% satisfaction guarantee. Whether you need regular pest service, termite inspections or help with one of those unexpected desert critters, Mr. Beez is thorough, professional and incredibly dependable. They are one of those companies I never hesitate to recommend because I know they will take great care of you - just like they have taken care of so many of my friends, clients and neighbors.

darceysTake: If you are buying a home, refinancing or simply need a fast, reliable pre-approval, I cannot recommend VanMar Lending enough. Kristen and Carlos are basically family to us, and they have handled our mortgage needs time and time again. We trust them completely because they consistently deliver exactly what they promise: honest advice, lightning-fast pre-approvals, outstanding communication and a smooth, stress-free lending experience from start to finish. Since 2012, they have helped countless families throughout the Coachella Valley with Conventional, FHA, VA, USDA and Jumbo loans, earning a reputation for exceptional service, creative solutions and keeping clients informed every step of the way. Their philosophy is simple: communicate clearly, solve problems quickly and get the job done on time. Whether you are a first-time buyer, purchasing your dream home or refinancing, you will be treated like family from your very first conversation. Their outstanding client reviews speak for themselves, but for us, it is even more personal. They are the only team we trust with our own mortgages, and we are confident they will take just as great care of you.
